Alright lads, Sick and tired of shitty, pozzed western games that suck black dicks, so I thought I would go back to and old favorite. Deus Ex.

Deus Ex as you all know was the daddy PC game back when it landed in the yr 2000, and some say still is.

I decided that I wanted to go back into the dystopian Cyberpunk world, but didn't want to experience it at the the rather blocky aesthetic that was pretty rough around the edges even back then. I hunted around for a graphics mods and found that a Dev team called Caustic Creative had put together a massive mod overhaul in the same vein as Elder scrolls 3: Morrowind rebirth.

Install was simple as fuck. You download the original game through steam, then download Revision mod (again through Steam). You launch the revision mod through steam and off you go. Good for a total tech 'tard like me.

Now I thought this was going to be a old game with a new lick of paint, but these guys have really gone to town. The Textures have a total overhaul, look really sweet in places. This was not a pretty game back in 2000, even amongst its peers. But now it is far more appealing to the eyeballs, except for the blocky nature of the architecture, but that is outside of the remit of a modder team.

As well environment textures, weapons have also been upgraded from the rather generic models of yesteryear, and certain upgrades found in the game now show on the weapon model once installed (scopes and lasers). The only textures that seem a bit...well, shit are the character and NPC's. They only spruced up major Characters (JC Denton and his brother etc, and these aren't very good) and the rest just got a 1080 overhaul. But from what I can gather this mod was nicked from someone else, and not done by Caustic Creative.

The game now also includes new environment assets. New trees, bushes, columns and shrubs. In the the more metropolitan hub levels the devs have slapped up a great deal of blade runner-esq neon advertisements (some with minimal animation) to bring a greater cyberpunk aesthetic and move away from the original games stark environmental design. Good shit if you ask me.

As for the levels themselves, the smaller ones aren't really any different, but the larger hub levels have had a bunch of cut contact inserted back into the game. So much so that someone like me that used to have a lovers knowledge of the game was completely lost once I hit the Hell's kitchen level.

On top of all this the devs have included a couple of mods called Shifter and Biomod that changes up the weapons stats, introduces new unique weapons and rebalances the skills and biomods (and allows you to swap out mods) I haven't played with them yet, but they can be turned on/off in game.

I highly recommend this bad boy mod for new players and veterans. If you have not played this game before, beware that you will get no hand holding or map markers in Deus Ex. His grandson, John Booth, Jr., (1723-1787), was a silversmith established in London, England. He married Elizabeth Wilkes (1720-1801); John's sons John and Philip founded a London distillery in 1740 and began selling Booth's dry gin, eventually becoming the largest gin distillery in the UK; while his son Richard (John Wilkes Booth's grandfather) was an attorney. Richard's son, Junius Brutus Booth (1796-1852), was a well-known Shakespearean actor in England and America.
